title: Criminal intimidation through social media - is it taken seriously enough
p1:
A threatening message online may look like “just words” — but what happens when those words create real fear?

Many people still believe that criminal intimidation only applies when someone threatens you face-to-face. That belief can be costly in the digital age.
p2:
Social media threats, repeated warnings, and messages designed to scare someone can have serious consequences. The surprising part is that the platform does not decide the seriousness — the intent behind the communication and the impact on the victim matter more.

A threat sent through a screen can still affect a person's safety, reputation, and mental peace.
p3:
The key lesson is simple: online behaviour is not automatically protected just because it happens digitally. Screenshots, timestamps, and message records can become important evidence when a threat crosses the line.

Think before posting, forwarding, or sending aggressive messages. Digital spaces still carry real-world responsibility.
conclusion: Do you think social media threats are treated as seriously as offline threats, or is more awareness needed?
